newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli prisoner release halted over court hearing.
newsitem.headline: Israeli prisoner release halted over court hearing.

text.p: A last-minute petition to Israel's High Court halted the release of Palestinian women prisoners on Tuesday after authorities freed several inmates under peace deals with the PLO.

A justice official said the release of the nine prisoners in question would be held up pending the court's discussion of the request by the "Families of Victims of Arab Terror" to halt the release of the nine, saying they were arrested after the Israel-PLO agreements and were not eligible for freedom.

Witnesses said eight Palestinian women were freed but police said several returned to prison on their own volition and the rest were refusing to leave until authorities allowed all 31 women inmates to leave.
A police spokeswoman said only three women slated for release were outside prison walls.

"The girls are refusing to leave without the rest of the nine prisoners. This is our position as well," said Ziad al-Atrash, the Palestinian head of the military district coordinating offices in the West Bank and Gaza.

Among the three was Lamya Maarouf, a 32-year-old Brazilian citizen released at about 4 p.m. (1400 GMT) from the prison in Tel Mond. Israeli and Palestinian officials said she would be deported to Brazil.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat waited in Ramallah to greet the women but they never arrived.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, paying hospital visits in the north to soldiers wounded in Lebanon, said the promise to free the women had been made originally by the previous Labour government.
"It's not a tactic, we are serious about fulfilling commitments, but we intend fully to see that there is an equal reciprocity on the other side," Netanyahu told reporters.

Israel has demanded the PLO keep its promise to change sections of the PLO charter calling for the destruction of the Jewish state, avoid political activity in Jerusalem and fight Palestinian guerrilla groups opposed to peace deals.
"Thirty-one Palestinian women will be released today, 25 from Hasharon prison and six from Neve Tirza prison," an Israeli police spokeswoman said earlier on Tuesday.
Maarouf was arrested in 1986 for driving the car in which Israeli soldier David Manos was kidnapped. Manos was killed and Maarouf was sentenced to 25 years in jail.

At least two other convicted killers were due to be released included Abeer al-Wheidy, 27, arrested in 1992 for belonging to a cell of the PLO's mainstream Fatah faction that killed a Jewish settler from the settlement of Ofra near Ramallah and May Ghussein, 23, arrested in 1991 for security reasons.
Ghussein confessed to killing a Palestinian in jail suspected of collaborating with the prison authorities.
PLO official Hisham Abdel Razek said that after the release one Palestinian female would remain behind bars in Israel -- a 15-year-old arrested two weeks ago trying to stab an Israeli soldier.
He said 28 of the women were convicted of security offences and three were jailed for criminal activity unrelated to the Israeli-Arab conflict.
The release of female, sick and young prisoners was a commitment made in a deal signed by the previous government in September 1995 with the Palestine Liberation Organisation.
Israel released some of the male sick and elderly prisoners but about 5,000 Palestinians are still in its prisons, Palestinian sources said.
